title: Fix DefaultParser keeping property values across parses
body:
If you reuse an `Options` instance and pass `Properties` to `DefaultParser.parse()`, the first parse leaves the property value behind in the `Option` registered in `Options`: `handleProperties()` called `processValue()` on that registered option rather than on the copy that goes into the `CommandLine`, and nothing ever clears it. From then on the same `Options` gives wrong answers:

- a later parse with a different property value still returns the first one;
- `-o value` on the command line returns the old property value, and `value` ends up in the argument list;
- with a `-D` style option (`hasArgs().valueSeparator('=')`), pairs from the earlier properties show up in the next parse's `getOptionProperties()`.

The fix adds the value to the copy instead, the same way values from the command line are handled, so parsing no longer changes the values of the registered options. A value the option already has still wins over the property, as `testPropertiesPreserveExistingOptionValue()` expects, and the `parse(Options, Properties, NonOptionAction, String...)` Javadoc now says so. The three new tests in `DefaultParserTest` fail on master and pass with the change.
